output.answer: Yes. Paramount — now part of Skydance Corp. following the $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery that closed October 6, 2026 — has announced that layoffs are coming: chairman/CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz told employees in a memo the morning the deal closed that 'difficult decisions that affect our workforce' would be part of the integration, and layoffs began this month, starting in the games division on November 9, 2026 (at least 30 people cut, per Insider Gaming). The company has not disclosed a total headcount for the new round; it has said layoffs will help drive at least $6 billion in cost savings over three years, and it began offering voluntary buyouts in October 2026 ahead of official layoffs. Separately, about 2,000 jobs were cut in October 2025 after the original Skydance–Paramount merger.
caveats: Skydance has disclosed no total headcount for the post-Warner Bros. Discovery job cuts, and no WARN notice or SEC restructuring filing has been published for this round as of November 11, 2026.
The widely circulated figure of about 2,000 jobs belongs to the separate October 2025 round that followed the Skydance Media–Paramount merger, not the Warner Bros. Discovery deal.
The exact number laid off in the games division is unclear; the 'at least 30' figure comes from Insider Gaming's report, and Skydance's statement did not give a number.
A Los Angeles County report in August estimated the merger could cost some 4,500 film and TV jobs in L.A. over three years, but that is a projection, not an announced cut.

passages.quote: "Integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce," the execs wrote in the memo, a copy of which was obtained by Variety. "We are committed to handling this process thoughtfully and respectfully."

Paramount execs have said they are shooting to achieve more than $6 billion in cost savings (reductions in operating costs on an annualized basis) within three years — and part of that will come from layoffs. The company has not revealed at this point the extent of the job cuts it expects.
Last month, Skydance began offering voluntary buyouts to employees ahead of official layoffs. At the same time, the company adopted a five-day-per-week in-office policy.
Skydance has begun laying off workers at Paramount Games. That's been expected since Paramount closed the $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros.
Insider Gaming reported that at least 30 people were let go in the cuts.
Skydance closed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, and told staff the same morning that job cuts were coming without attaching a single number to them.

output.question: Has Paramount announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: Skydance closed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on October 6, 2026, and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz sent employees a memo the same morning acknowledging layoffs would follow the integration, without giving a headcount.
In October 2026 Skydance began offering voluntary buyouts to employees ahead of official layoffs and simultaneously adopted a five-day-per-week in-office policy.
Layoffs began in the games division: Skydance confirmed layoffs at Paramount Games/Skydance Games on November 9, 2026, with at least 30 people let go per Insider Gaming; no total number was given.

Skydance outlined at least $6 billion in cost savings over three years on November 9, 2026, including at least $2.2 billion from eliminating redundant back-office and corporate functions (management layers, AI, office footprint) — layoffs are part of how those savings will be achieved, but no headcount was disclosed.
About 2,000 jobs were cut in a separate October 2025 round that followed the $8 billion Skydance Media merger with Paramount.
A Los Angeles County report issued in August estimated the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger could result in the loss of some 4,500 film and TV jobs over three years in L.A. alone.
